questions.prompt: The brave soldiers are praised by the general because they defended the fatherland.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs fortēs ā duce laudantur quod patriam dēfendērunt.

questions.prompt: You were being blamed by everyone, although you had committed no crime.
questions.answer: Ab omnibus culpābāris, quamquam nūllum scelus commīserās.

questions.prompt: We shall be called back to the city when the war has been finished.
questions.answer: In urbem revocābimur, cum bellum cōnfectum erit.

questions.prompt: Let the captives be freed, so that peace may be preserved.
questions.answer: Captīvī līberentur, ut pāx cōnservētur.

questions.prompt: The road to the camp was shown to the strangers by a shepherd.
questions.answer: Via ad castra ā pāstōre hospitibus mōnstrāta est.

questions.prompt: That boy is named after his grandfather, whom everyone loved.
questions.answer: Ille puer ex avō appellātur, quem omnēs amābant.

questions.prompt: You will be greeted by the citizens as you enter the forum.
questions.answer: Ā cīvibus salūtāberis, dum forum intrās.

questions.prompt: The enemy having been conquered, the town was occupied by our men.
questions.answer: Hostibus superātīs, oppidum ā nostrīs occupātum est.

questions.prompt: Many soldiers were being wounded while the walls were being stormed.
questions.answer: Multī mīlitēs vulnerābantur, dum moenia oppugnantur.

questions.prompt: The city will be stormed unless the gates are opened at once.
questions.answer: Urbs expugnābitur, nisi portae statim aperientur.

questions.prompt: May the fatherland never be conquered by a cruel enemy!
questions.answer: Numquam patria ab hoste crūdēlī superētur!

questions.prompt: The spoils were being carried through the streets by the triumphant soldiers.
questions.answer: Spolia per viās ā mīlitibus triumphantibus portābantur.

questions.prompt: This story will be told to the children, so that they may be moved by virtue.
questions.answer: Haec fābula līberīs nārrābitur, ut virtūte moveantur.

questions.prompt: If the fields had been laid waste, the farmers would have been overwhelmed by hunger.
questions.answer: Sī agrī vāstātī essent, agricolae fame obrutī essent.

questions.prompt: The fields were being watered by streams flowing down from the mountains.
questions.answer: Agrī rīvīs dē montibus dēfluentibus rigābantur.

questions.prompt: Tomorrow you will be summoned to the assembly by the leader.
questions.answer: Ad concilium ā duce crās vocāberis.

questions.prompt: If the gods were honored, the city would be preserved by them.
questions.answer: Sī deī colerentur, urbs ab eīs servārētur.

questions.prompt: We are being watched by the guards standing at the gate.
questions.answer: Ā custōdibus ad portam stantibus spectāmur.

questions.prompt: The new law had been approved by the senate with great applause.
questions.answer: Nova lēx ā senātū magnō plausū comprobāta erat.

questions.prompt: Let the boundaries of the fields be marked by these stones.
questions.answer: Fīnēs agrōrum hīs lapidibus signentur.

questions.prompt: The wise man is often praised, but he is rarely celebrated by the common crowd.
questions.answer: Sapiēns saepe laudātur, sed rārō ā vulgō celebrātur.

questions.prompt: While the city was being besieged, the walls were being strengthened by the anxious citizens.
questions.answer: Dum urbs oppugnābātur, mūrī ā cīvibus sollicitīs firmābantur.

questions.prompt: If the truth had been hidden, the citizens would have been tempted by false words.
questions.answer: Nisi vēritās occultāta esset, cīvēs falsīs verbīs temptātī essent.

questions.prompt: Let the household gods be worshipped, so that the family may be preserved from every danger.
questions.answer: Penātēs adōrentur, ut familia ab omnī perīculō cōnservētur.

questions.prompt: The exhausted farmer is being cared for by his neighbors, until he recovers his strength.
questions.answer: Agricola dēfessus ā vīcīnīs cūrātur, dōnec convalēscat.

questions.prompt: You will be accused of avarice, unless the money is put back in the temple.
questions.answer: Avāritiae accūsāberis, nisi pecūnia templō repōnātur.

questions.prompt: The camp had been fortified by the soldiers before the enemy was announced.
questions.answer: Castra ā mīlitibus firmāta erant, priusquam hostis nūntiārētur.

questions.prompt: Let the greedy merchant be watched, however sweetly he speaks.
questions.answer: Mercātor avārus observētur, quamvīs suāviter loquātur.

questions.prompt: The spoils taken from the enemy are being carried into the city by rejoicing soldiers.
questions.answer: Spolia ab hoste capta ā mīlitibus laetantibus in urbem portantur.

questions.prompt: We were being watched by silent guards while the treaty was being discussed.
questions.answer: Ā custōdibus tacitīs spectābāmur, dum foedus tractābātur.

questions.prompt: The frugal old man will be praised by all, because nothing is consumed in his house.
questions.answer: Senex parcus ab omnibus laudābitur, quod nihil in domō eius cōnsūmitur.

questions.prompt: If the fields were watered by gentle rains, the harvest would be doubled.
questions.answer: Sī agrī lēnibus imbribus irrigārentur, messis duplicārētur.

questions.prompt: You are being blamed by the crowd, although your innocence is known to all.
questions.answer: Ā vulgō culpāris, quamquam innocentia tua omnibus nōta est.

questions.prompt: The ancient temple will be renewed, so that the gods may be honored again.
questions.answer: Templum antīquum renovābitur, ut deī iterum honōrentur.

questions.prompt: The traitor had been condemned by the senate before the crime was made public.
questions.answer: Prōditor ā senātū damnātus erat, priusquam scelus vulgārētur.

questions.prompt: Let these boundary stones never be moved, lest discord be stirred up among neighbors.
questions.answer: Hī terminī numquam moveantur, nē discordia inter vīcīnōs excitētur.

questions.prompt: The shipwrecked sailors were freed from the waves by a passing fisherman.
questions.answer: Nautae naufragī ā piscātōre praetereunte ē flūctibus līberātī sunt.

questions.prompt: You will be summoned before the judge, unless the debt is paid quickly.
questions.answer: Ad iūdicem citāberis, nisi aes aliēnum celeriter solvātur.

questions.prompt: The lazy servants are reproached daily, but they are corrected by no punishment.
questions.answer: Servī ignāvī cotīdiē vituperantur, sed nūllā poenā ēmendantur.

questions.prompt: The bridge having been destroyed, the fleeing troops were saved by the swift river.
questions.answer: Ponte dēlētō, cōpiae fugientēs rapidō flūmine servātae sunt.
